raw_case_text:
A 65-year-old married male, office worker,diagnosed with HIV in 2011 (baseline CD4+ count: 84 cells/microl; initial viral load undocumented), was initially treated with AZT/3TC/NVP. He switched to bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide in May 2022. In March 2022, he developed painless lymphadenopathy in the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions, with the largest node being chestnut-sized, firm, smooth, and mobile. There was no fever, erythema, discharge, or skin adhesion. The patient did not seek medical care initially.
On June 18, 2022, he presented to Tianjin Second People's Hospital with mildly enlarged cervical nodes. A biopsy on June 22 suggested reactive hyperplasia. PET-CT on June 29 revealed widespread lymphadenopathy with elevated FDG uptake, based on diffuse, symmetric nodal uptake and absence of focal destructive lesions, including bilateral cervical (max SUV 11.03), axillary (max SUV 10.03), thoracic, abdominal, and inguinal nodes(Figure 1). Although lymphoma was suspected, inflammatory changes were considered more likely. The patient received treatment with glucocorticoids. and was discharged with follow-up advice.
He returned on July 4 with new-onset fever (up to 39.5  C), fatigue, anorexia, chest tightness, dyspnea, and progressive lymph node enlargement. Repeat lymph node puncture again indicated reactive proliferation. Bone marrow biopsy with histopathological examination and flow cytometry, which showed no lymphoma infiltration. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of lymph node tissue detected HHV-8 and EBV. Symptoms improved with anti-infective and glucocorticoid therapy, and he was discharged after lymph node regression. On August 27, he was readmitted with recurrent high fever and worsening lymphadenopathy, prompting referral to our hospital.
Physical examination at admission showed enlarged, firm, non-tender, mobile lymph nodes in the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions:the largest being egg-sized:without erythema or ulceration. Vital signs were stable, and systemic examination was otherwise normal.
Lab tests showed a CD4+ count of 435 cells/microl, CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.44, and undetectable HIV viral load. Notable findings included thrombocytopenia (85x109/L), mild anemia (Hb 118 g/L), and elevated inflammatory markers: ESR 69 mm/h, CRP 68.33 mg/L, and IL-6 21.86 pg/mL. Liver and kidney function were normal. Syphilis serology was positive (TPPA+, RPR 1:2). EBV IgG positive, EBV DNA negative. Chest CT suggested possible lymph node space-occupying lesions. Abdominal CT revealed splenomegaly, retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy, and a cystic lesion in the right inguinal region.
After the results of the puncture biopsy could not confirm the diagnosis, a resection biopsy was eventually performed to make a definite diagnosis. Excisional biopsy of cervical and inguinal nodes confirmed the diagnosis: histology showed follicular hyperplasia with mantle zone expansion exhibiting an "onion-skin" pattern, vascular proliferation, and HHV-8 positivity on immunohistochemistry. These findings supported HHV-8+ multicentric Castleman disease, plasma cell type (Figures 2, 3).
The patient was diagnosed with HIV-associated HHV-8+ multicentric Castleman disease and latent syphilis. Treatment began on September 22, 2022, with four weekly cycles of rituximab (375 mg/m2) and etoposide (100 mg/m2). Syphilis was treated with benzathine penicillin G (2.4 million units IM weekly for three weeks).Persist in using bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide for HIV treatment.
A follow-up PET-CT scan in January 2023 revealed significant therapeutic improvement, characterized by a marked reduction in the size and number of lymph nodes across all previously involved regions, along with substantially decreased FDG uptake (SUVmax 2.52, mean 1.76), indicating an excellent treatment response (Figure 4). Throughout 36 months of continuous monitoring, the patient has maintained sustained complete remission with no evidence of disease recurrence (Table 1).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 65-year-old married male office worker with HIV presented with a 5-month history of progressive generalized lymphadenopathy and a 2-month history of recurrent high fevers (up to 39.5 °C), fatigue, anorexia, chest tightness, and dyspnea.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In March 2022, the patient noticed painless, mobile, chestnut-sized cervical, axillary, and inguinal lymphadenopathy. In June 2022, initial fine-needle/core biopsy suggested reactive hyperplasia and FDG-PET/CT (June 29, 2022) showed diffuse hypermetabolic lymphadenopathy (cervical SUVmax 11.03, axillary SUVmax 10.03), transiently improving with glucocorticoids. On July 4, 2022, and again on August 27, 2022, he was hospitalized with recurrent high fevers up to 39.5 °C, fatigue, anorexia, chest tightness, dyspnea, and progressive nodal enlargement to egg size.
subjective.past_medical_history: Diagnosed with HIV infection in 2011 (baseline CD4+ count 84 cells/µL), treated initially with zidovudine/lamivudine/nevirapine (AZT/3TC/NVP) and switched in May 2022 to bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for recurrent high fever (up to 39.5 °C), fatigue, anorexia, chest tightness, dyspnea, and generalized painless lymphadenopathy. Home medication: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide.

objective.physical_examination: Vital signs were stable on admission; physical examination revealed multiple enlarged (up to egg-sized), firm, smooth, mobile, non-tender cervical, axillary, and inguinal lymph nodes without overlying erythema, ulceration, or skin adherence.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission blood tests showed mild anemia (hemoglobin 118 g/L), thrombocytopenia (platelets 85 x 10^9/L), normal hepatic and renal function, elevated ESR (69 mm/h), elevated CRP (68.33 mg/L), and elevated IL-6 (21.86 pg/mL). Syphilis serology was positive (TPPA positive, RPR titer 1:2); EBV IgG was positive with negative plasma EBV DNA.
objective.advanced_workup: Admission CD4+ T-cell count was 435 cells/µL with a CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.44. Baseline FDG-PET/CT showed diffuse symmetric hypermetabolic cervical, axillary, thoracic, abdominal, and inguinal lymphadenopathy; chest and abdominal CT showed nodal enlargement, splenomegaly, and a right inguinal cystic lesion. Bone marrow biopsy and flow cytometry excluded lymphoma, while lymph node mNGS detected HHV-8 and EBV. Excisional biopsy of cervical and inguinal lymph nodes confirmed HHV-8-positive multicentric Castleman disease (plasma cell type), demonstrating follicular hyperplasia with 'onion-skin' mantle zone expansion, interfollicular vascular proliferation, plasma cell sheets, and HHV-8 immunohistochemical positivity.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: HIV-associated HHV-8-positive multicentric Castleman disease (MCD, plasma cell variant) and concurrent latent syphilis in a 65-year-old male with virologically suppressed HIV infection (undetectable plasma HIV viral load, CD4+ count 435 cells/µL, CD4/CD8 ratio 0.44 on bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide). Confirmed via excisional cervical and inguinal lymph node histopathology, HHV-8 immunohistochemistry, and nodal mNGS after two prior needle biopsies showed nonspecific reactive hyperplasia. Starting September 22, 2022, he was treated with four weekly cycles of intravenous rituximab (375 mg/m2) plus etoposide (100 mg/m2) alongside intramuscular benzathine penicillin G (2.4 million units weekly for 3 weeks for latent syphilis) and continued bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide. Follow-up PET-CT in January 2023 demonstrated marked nodal regression and metabolic resolution (SUVmax reduced from 11.03 to 2.52), and the patient maintained complete remission over 36 months of follow-up.
